data.name: Julien
data.gender_notes: Julien is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin JULIANUS, derived from JULIUS, meaning 'youthful, downy-bearded'. The name Julien is of Latin origin and is used mainly in the French-speaking world. The name Julien carries the meaning “Youthful, downy-bearded” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Julien usually hope their child will grow to embody youthful, downy-bearded and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Julien belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Youthful, downy-bearded.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Julien total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Julien
in_english.long_meaning: The name Julien originates from the Latin Julianus, meaning descended from youth or youthful. It is associated with the Roman family name Iulius, symbolizing vigor and new beginnings. Historically, Julien conveys spiritual renewal and a connection to early Christian traditions.

data.cultural_impact: Julien is a name deeply rooted in French and Roman history. The name Julien was popular among the early Christians in France, and several notable saints and heroes bear this name, which in turn has influenced its enduring popularity in the country. For centuries, the name Julien has been associated with strength, courage, and nobility, making it a sought-after name for boys in French-speaking families.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Julien can be traced back to its original Latin root, JULIANUS, which means 'youthful' or 'downy-bearded'. In the Christian faith, this name is often associated with the Child Jesus, symbolizing the innocence, purity, and divinity of the infant Savior. Additionally, several Christian saints and martyrs with the name Julien have left a lasting impression on the faith and culture, serving as models of faith, courage, and devotion for generations. Thus, for many Christians, the name Julien carries spiritual significance as a reminder of the youthful, innocent, and divine nature of God and His love for us.
